title: Semilinear coherence of unit-normalized derived-colimit exchange
statement:
Let $\mathcal E,\mathcal D$ be small categories with identity-cover topologies and let $u:\mathcal E\to\mathcal D$ be a functor. Let $\alpha:R\to S$, $\alpha':R'\to S'$, $a:R\to R'$ and $b:S\to S'$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings with $b\alpha=\alpha'a$. Use module presheaves, their ordinary unbounded derived categories, exact constants $C$ and derived colimits $L_{\mathcal E,R},L_{\mathcal E,S},L_{\mathcal D,R'},L_{\mathcal D,S'}$ of [lem-trf-derived-colimit-bar]. Precomposition $u^{-1}$ and scalar restriction are applied termwise [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Write $T_{\mathcal E,\alpha}$ and $T_{*,\alpha}$ for derived coefficient extension on presheaves and on point modules, respectively [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], and similarly for $(\mathcal D,\alpha')$. Use the tensor--restriction adjunctions of [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]. Suppose
$$\chi_{\mathcal E,\alpha}:L_{\mathcal E,S}T_{\mathcal E,\alpha}\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{*,\alpha}L_{\mathcal E,R}$$
and $\chi_{\mathcal D,\alpha'}$ are the unique natural isomorphisms of left adjoints normalized by the equality of right adjoints $r_{\mathcal E}C_S=C_Rr_*$, with composite units as in [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction, lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation]. For $M\in D(\underline R_{\mathcal E})$, $M'\in D(\underline{R'}_{\mathcal D})$ and $t:M\to\operatorname{Res}_a u^{-1}M'$, define $a_R:L_{\mathcal E,R}M\to\operatorname{Res}_aL_{\mathcal D,R'}M'$ by transposing $t$ followed by the colimit unit of $M'$. Define $t_S:T_{\mathcal E,\alpha}M\to\operatorname{Res}_b u^{-1}T_{\mathcal D,\alpha'}M'$ by transposing $t$ followed by the coefficient-extension unit of $M'$, using $b\alpha=\alpha'a$ to identify the restrictions. Let $a_S$ be its semilinear derived-colimit map. Define $b_R:T_{*,\alpha}L_{\mathcal E,R}M\to\operatorname{Res}_bT_{*,\alpha'}L_{\mathcal D,R'}M'$ by transposing $a_R$ followed by the point coefficient-extension unit. Then
$$\operatorname{Res}_b(\chi_{\mathcal D,\alpha'}(M'))\circ a_S=b_R\circ\chi_{\mathcal E,\alpha}(M)$$
in $D(S)$. These equations respect identity maps, composition of indexing functors, and pasting of coefficient-ring squares, with the canonical adjoint composition identifications inserted.
For ordinary module presheaves $F,G$ and an $a$-semilinear natural map $t:F\to u^{-1}G$, the termwise chain isomorphisms $\Phi_{\mathcal E,\alpha}:K_{\mathcal E,S}(F\otimes_R S)\to K_{\mathcal E,R}(F)\otimes_R S$ and $\Phi_{\mathcal D,\alpha'}$, specified by $(\sigma,x\otimes s)\mapsto(\sigma,x)\otimes s$, satisfy the same square on complexes: the tensor map sends $x\otimes s$ to $t(x)\otimes b(s)$ and both composites send $(\sigma,x\otimes s)$ to $(u\sigma,t(x))\otimes b(s)$. This chain-level assertion needs no flatness; whenever the displayed tensors are K-flat derived representatives it represents the preceding derived square.

proof.text: Write $P=\operatorname{Res}_a u^{-1}$ on $R'$-presheaves and $Q=\operatorname{Res}_b u^{-1}$ on $S'$-presheaves. Write $r_E,r_D,r_*$ for restriction along $\alpha,\alpha',\alpha$ respectively, $\lambda_{E,R},\lambda_{D,R'},\lambda_{E,S},\lambda_{D,S'}$ for the colimit units, and $\tau_E,\tau_D,\tau_*,\tau_*'$ for the tensor units. All units are in the ordinary unbounded derived categories. Exact precomposition commutes with constants and restriction termwise; $P r_D=r_EQ$ follows because both scalar actions are through $b\alpha=\alpha'a$. Put $A_E=L_{E,S}T_{E,\alpha}$, $B_E=T_{*,\alpha}L_{E,R}$, $V_E=r_EC_{E,S}=C_{E,R}r_*$. Composite adjunction gives $A_E\dashv V_E$ with unit $\eta_{A,E}=r_E\lambda_{E,S}\circ\tau_E$, and $B_E\dashv V_E$ with unit $\eta_{B,E}=C_{E,R}\tau_*\circ\lambda_{E,R}$; use primed analogues on $D$. The specified normalization is precisely $V_E(\chi_E)\eta_{A,E}=\eta_{B,E}$ and its $D$ analogue.

proof.text:
Set $Z=\operatorname{Res}_bB_DM'$. Transpose the left side of the desired equality under $A_E\dashv V_E$. By definition of $a_S$, $C_{E,S}(a_S)\lambda_{E,S}=Q(\lambda_{D,S'})t_S$. By definition of $t_S$, $r_E(t_S)\tau_E=P(\tau_D)t$. Consequently this transpose is
$$r_EC_{E,S}(\operatorname{Res}_b\chi_D)\,r_EQ(\lambda_{D,S'})\,P(\tau_D)t
=P\bigl(r_DC_{D,S'}(\chi_D)\,r_D(\lambda_{D,S'})\tau_D\bigr)t
=P(\eta_{B,D})t:M\longrightarrow V_EZ.$$
Here restrictions of point modules and constants commute literally on complexes, and then on their derived categories. The last equality is the unit-normalization equation for $\chi_D$. This argument concerns arbitrary derived morphisms $t$, without choosing a chain representative.

proof.text:
The right side has transpose $V_E(b_R)\eta_{B,E}$, by the normalization for $\chi_E$. The defining transposes of $b_R$ and $a_R$ say
$$r_*(b_R)\tau_*=\operatorname{Res}_a(\tau_*')a_R,\qquad C_{E,R}(a_R)\lambda_{E,R}=P(\lambda_{D,R'})t.$$
Thus its transpose is
$$C_{E,R}(\operatorname{Res}_a\tau_*')\,C_{E,R}(a_R)\lambda_{E,R}
=P\bigl(C_{D,R'}(\tau_*')\lambda_{D,R'}\bigr)t
=P(\eta_{B,D})t.$$
The Hom bijection of the composite adjunction is injective. Steps 2 and 3 therefore prove the asserted equality in $D(S)$, with source $A_EM$ and target $Z$.

proof.text: For composable indexing/ring data write $P_1,P_2$ for the two restrictions with precomposition and $t_1,t_2$ for the two input arrows. The composite input is $P_1(t_2)t_1$. Naturality of the intervening colimit unit makes the transpose of the composite colimit arrows exactly $P_1P_2(\lambda_3)P_1(t_2)t_1$, the defining transpose for the composite input. The same calculation with $\tau_3$ instead of $\lambda_3$ proves composition for coefficient-extension transposes. Identity inputs give the units themselves and hence identity adjuncts. For pasting coefficient squares, restriction along a composite ring map is iterated restriction, so the two right-adjoint squares paste to the same equality. Apply the two pasting formulas for mates: pasting along the indexing functors uses clause 1, and pasting along coefficient adjunctions uses clause 2. The composite units are exactly those of step 1, so the pasted normalized comparisons equal the single normalized comparison by uniqueness. Clause 4 gives identities. This supplies the canonical adjoint composition identifications required in the statement, rather than requiring them to be strict equalities of left adjoints.

proof.text:
For ordinary presheaves the coefficient map on tensors exists without flatness: additivity is immediate, and balancing holds since
$$t(rx)\otimes b(s)=a(r)t(x)\otimes b(s)=t(x)\otimes\alpha'(a(r))b(s)=t(x)\otimes b(\alpha(r)s).$$
This defines the $b$-semilinear map $x\otimes s\mapsto t(x)\otimes b(s)$. Naturality of $t$ makes it commute with every presheaf restriction. For each chain-indexed direct sum, define $\Phi(\sigma,x\otimes s)=(\sigma,x)\otimes s$. Its inverse is the balanced map $(\sum_\sigma(\sigma,x_\sigma))\otimes s\mapsto\sum_\sigma(\sigma,x_\sigma\otimes s)$; all sums here are finite. The two composites are identities on the displayed generators, which generate the modules. Hence these are mutually inverse linear maps in every degree.

proof.text: The bar faces delete the same vertex on both sides of $\Phi$. All but the last face keep the coefficient, while the last face restricts it. Since restrictions on $F\otimes_R S$ send $x\otimes s$ to $x|_V\otimes s$, every face commutes with $\Phi$, and hence so does their signed sum. Thus $\Phi$ is a chain isomorphism. The bar map for $(u,t)$ sends $(\sigma,x)$ to $(u\sigma,t(x))$. Around either route of the claimed square its tensor version therefore sends $(\sigma,x\otimes s)$ to $(u\sigma,t(x))\otimes b(s)$. Equality on these generators proves equality of chain maps, including degree zero and zero terms. No exactness of tensor was used.

source.place: Tags 08PH (example-morphism-categories), 08Q8 (lemma-change-of-rings); agent expansion of the semilinear compatibility by composite Hom bijections.

proof.text: Finally suppose these tensors are K-flat derived representatives. For an ordinary presheaf $F$, K-flatness of $F[0]$ forces each $F(U)$ to be flat: tensor $F[0]$ with the constant three-term complex of any short exact sequence of $R$-modules and evaluate at $U$. Its acyclicity says exactly that this short exact sequence stays exact after tensoring with $F(U)$. The same applies to $G$. The objectwise-flat bar lemma now gives flat terms and canonical K-flat comparisons for both bar complexes. The bar-unit-transpose lemma identifies each $\Phi^{-1}$ with the unique unit-normalized comparison $B\to A$, so each $\Phi$ represents the specified $\chi$. The representative-normalized tensor adjunction sends $x$ to $x\otimes1$; its adjunct formula sends $x\otimes s$ to $s$ times the input map. Applied to $t$ and the unit of $G$, it gives exactly $t(x)\otimes b(s)$. The bar theorem identifies the other arrows with $(\sigma,x)\mapsto(u\sigma,t(x))$. Consequently the chain square of step 6 represents the derived square of steps 2--3 whenever these K-flat computations apply.
